commit_message:
[Merged] [string] Optimize and refactor index hashing

gotos are considered harmful and switches are not, so extract out
helper functions from index hashing which report whether the index
contained non-index (non-digit or leading zero) values, or whether it
simply overflowed.

Also do some microoptimisation that merges the index check with the
conversion to decimal, and changes the overflow check to detect overflow
(with a single branch) rather than prevent it (with branches dependent
on both the current digit and the value so far). This should reduce
branches and tighten the loop.

fix_commit_message:
[string] Fix overflow case of TryParseArrayIndex

The "undo" on overflow was undoing the overflowing add, but not the
overflowing multiplication, which is lossy and not undoable. This is
probably being too clever -- on 64-bit platforms, where this overflow
can happen, we can just have a 64-bit index variable and arithmetic on
it will still be cheap. On 32-bit platforms, we can keep the clever
check in order to keep a 32-bit value (and cheap 32-bit arithmetic);
these don't need an overflow case here anyway.

Drive-by fix a lint error with anonymous namespaces in a header.

Fixed: 395053819

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix f99c2e013acc on top of intro dcbc9e746073 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow):  Root cause: The `index` variable was typed as `uint32_t` even on 64-bit platforms where integer indices can legitimately exceed 32-bit range before the overflow boundary is reached. When `10 * index` wraps a 32-bit integer, information is permanently lost; the subsequent subtraction-based undo cannot reconstruct the original value. The overflow detection condition (`index + 1 < kMinValidValue + 1`) also fails to catch all overflow cases where the wrapped result accidentally falls within the valid uint32_t range.
